title: Verbalized and Internal Probabilities Are Coupled in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.00827v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models carry an internal notion of uncertainty in their sampling distribution, i.e., the probabilities they place on generating one answer rather than another. They can also be asked to state a confidence, in words or as a number: a verbalized uncertainty. Prior work suggests that internal probabilities track relative frequencies in the training data, and that verbalized probabilities track explicit probabilistic assertions in the training data. However, we do not know whether these two readouts are aligned, except when frequencies and probabilistic assertions in the training data happen to align. This limits our understanding of when we can use verbalized uncertainties as a proxy for either training data frequencies, or a model's internal distribution. We resolve this gap by systematically exploring how LLMs probability readouts are impacted by training and in-context data, via intervening on the underlying uncertainty

translated_title: 大语言模型中言语化概率与内部概率相互耦合
translated_abstract: 大语言模型在其采样分布中携带着一种内部的不确定性概念，即它们对生成某个答案而非另一个答案所赋予的概率。它们也可以被要求以文字或数字的形式陈述置信度：即言语化的不确定性。先前的研究表明，内部概率追踪训练数据中的相对频率，而言语化概率追踪训练数据中的显式概率陈述。然而，我们尚不清楚这两种读出方式是否相互一致，除非训练数据中的频率和概率陈述恰好吻合。这限制了我们对何时可以将言语化不确定性用作训练数据频率或模型内部分布的代理的理解。我们通过干预底层不确定性，系统地探索了训练数据和上下文内数据如何影响大语言模型的概率读出，从而填补了这一空白。
tldr: 该研究通过干预底层不确定性，系统揭示了大语言模型的内部概率（采样分布）与言语化概率（口头表达的置信度）是相互耦合的。
en_tdlr: This study systematically reveals, by intervening on underlying uncertainty, that internal probabilities (sampling distributions) and verbalized probabilities (stated confidence) are coupled in large language models.
